title: The Lost Ring
story:
James walked slowly over the crunching gravel, his fingers tightly gripping the heavy metal ring. Here, the world was made of hard lines and sharp corners, entirely unlike the soft, curving boughs of the Great Canopy. He had never felt ground so cold and unyielding under his knuckles. He had never smelled air so sharp with coal and grease. He had never seen shapes so aggressively straight.

As he crept between two towering walls of rusted iron, a sudden, thunderous clang shattered the silence nearby. A door had swung open at the far end of the alley. Startled, James let go of his metal ring. He watched, dismayed, as the heavy band rolled away, bouncing once, twice, before slipping cleanly through an iron grate in the dirt. It vanished into the dark earth with a hollow splash, gone beyond his reach.

James squeezed his eyes shut, momentarily panicked by the loss of his only possession. He breathed in, listening to calm his racing heart. He heard the drip of water below the grate. He heard the distant, low hum of the town's machinery. He heard the soft, heavy thud of approaching footsteps. One, two, three sounds. His breathing slowed, and he opened his eyes.

At the end of the alley stood a figure. It was incredibly tall, walking upright on two long limbs, draped in thick, dark fabric. A human. The figure did not see James, turning instead to latch a wooden shutter. James pressed himself against the rusted wall, his chest tight. But as the figure paused under a glowing yellow lantern, James took a soft breath and offered his customary salute to the unknown. "Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next," he whispered into the shadows.
location: A narrow alleyway inside the human town
